# Under --lang go the user's functions are emitted into the gomobile module,
# exported and capitalised, and emitIR does not emit them as Kotlin. So a Kotlin
# call site has to name them there. It did not: the module held `func Fib` and
# the Kotlin called a bare `fib(k)`, defined in neither file.
#
# fib recurses, so the inliner cannot fold it away -- which is what made this
# reachable at all, and why a non-recursive fixture would prove nothing.

sngl generate --lang go --platform android --out out app.sngl

# The module exports it.
grep 'func Fib\(n int\) int' out/golib/golib.go

# The Kotlin calls it there, and imports it.
grep 'golib\.Golib\.Fib\(k\)' out/MainScreen.kt
grep 'import golib\.Golib' out/MainScreen.kt

# Not as a bare local function, which is what used to be emitted.
! grep '= fib\(' out/MainScreen.kt
! grep 'fun fib' out/MainScreen.kt

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

func fib(n int) int {
    if n < 2 { return n }
    return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2)
}

component main {
    var k int = 10
    text(value=string(fib(k)))
    button(text="+", @click { k = k + 1 })
}
